Scene Representation Networks

Pixels supervise a continuous 3D world

NeurIPS 2019 · Oral, Outstanding New Directions — Vincent Sitzmann · Michael Zollhöfer · Gordon Wetzstein

TL;DR — a coordinate MLP stores scene geometry and appearance; a learned differentiable ray marcher turns posed RGB images into 3D supervision.

world point x
feature v
RGB
$$\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{3}\!\to\!\mathbb{R}^{n},\quad \mathbf{x}\mapsto\Phi(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{v}$$
$$d_{i+1}=d_i+\delta_i,\quad \delta_i=\mathrm{LSTM}(\Phi(\mathbf{r}(d_i)),h_i,c_i)$$
2D → 3D

50 posed RGB views across ~2.5k cars produce explicit normals and multi-view-consistent novel views — with no depth labels.

learned shape prior

02
SIREN

Sine makes every derivative learnable

NeurIPS 2020 · Oral — Vincent Sitzmann* · Julien N. P. Martel* · Alexander W. Bergman · David B. Lindell · Gordon Wetzstein

TL;DR — periodic activations fit high-frequency signals while keeping first- and higher-order derivatives expressive and analytically accessible.

$$\phi_i(\mathbf{x}_i)=\sin(\mathbf{W}_i\mathbf{x}_i+\mathbf{b}_i)$$
$$\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\sin(\omega x)=\omega\cos(\omega x)$$
+10 dB

Higher image-fitting PSNR than baseline MLPs; SIREN alone recovers accurate first and second derivatives.

optimization race
same coordinates, different activations
Periodic implicit representationWHY IT MATTERS · PDEs become trainable objectives
03
Light Field Networks

Skip marching: render each ray once

NeurIPS 2021 · Spotlight — Vincent Sitzmann* · Semon Rezchikov* · William T. Freeman · Joshua B. Tenenbaum · Frédo Durand

TL;DR — encode the 360° light field directly: each oriented ray maps to radiance in one MLP evaluation, while derivatives retain geometry.

point p
ray (d,m)
color c
$$\mathbf{r}=(\mathbf{d},\mathbf{m}),\quad \mathbf{m}=\mathbf{p}\times\mathbf{d}$$
$$\Phi_{\varphi}:\mathcal{L}\to\mathbb{R}^{3},\quad \mathbf{r}\mapsto\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r})$$
>500 FPS

One evaluation per ray enables real-time rendering — about 15,000× faster than PixelNeRF in the project comparison.

single-evaluation rendering
LFN vs PixelNeRF
Plücker-parameterized 4D light fieldWHY IT MATTERS · neural rendering becomes interactive

MetaSDF

Learn the initialization, then adapt in five steps

NeurIPS 2020 — Vincent Sitzmann* · Eric R. Chan* · Richard Tucker · Noah Snavely · Gordon Wetzstein

TL;DR — treat every shape as a task and meta-learn the SDF parameters plus per-parameter step sizes for rapid specialization.

θ
step 1
…
φ⁵
$$\phi_i^{j+1}=\phi_i^j-\alpha\odot\nabla_{\phi_i^j}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{train}},\quad \phi_i^0=\theta$$
$$\min_{\theta,\alpha}\sum_i\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{test}}\!\left(\Phi(\cdot;\phi_i^5)\right)$$
8s → 0.4s

ShapeNet test-time fitting is more than an order of magnitude faster than DeepSDF, with comparable reconstruction quality.
